skill.name: product-marketing
skill.description: Use when creating or updating product marketing context, ICP, positioning, and messaging foundations so the agent follows the marketingskills playbook instead of producing generic marketing advice.
whenToUse: The user asks for help creating or updating product marketing context, ICP, positioning, and messaging foundations
A marketing task needs product, audience, positioning, and channel context before execution
The agent should create a repeatable product marketing workflow instead of a one-off generic answer
The work needs clear success metrics, deliverables, and next steps for a growth or GTM motion

keyConcepts.explanation: First, check if .agents/product-marketing.md already exists. Also check .claude/product-marketing.md and the legacy filename product-marketing-context.md (in either .agents/ or .claude/) for older setups — if found anywhere other than .agents/product-marketing.md, offer to move it to the canonical location.
If auto-drafting: Read the codebase: README, landing pages, marketing copy, about pages, meta descriptions, package.json, any existing docs Draft all sections based on what you find
Core part of the product marketing workflow; use it to keep the agent focused on concrete marketing inputs, decisions, and outputs instead of vague recommendations.
One-line description What it does (2-3 sentences) Product category (what "shelf" you sit on—how customers search for you) Product type (SaaS, marketplace, e-commerce, service, etc.)
Target company type (industry, size, stage) Target decision-makers (roles, departments) Primary use case (the main problem you solve) Jobs to be done (2-3 things customers "hire" you for)

If multiple stakeholders are involved in buying, capture for each: User, Champion, Decision Maker, Financial Buyer, Technical Influencer What each cares about, their challenge, and the value you promise them

apiReference.purpose: Install the product-marketing skill from coreyhaines31/marketingskills.

gotchas: Keep the canonical context in .agents/product-marketing.md so every other marketing skill can reuse it.
Do not polish positioning language before collecting target audience, switching triggers, proof, and objections.
Read product-marketing context first when present; otherwise the agent may ask repeated setup questions or make weak positioning assumptions.
Do not ship generic best practices without tying recommendations to the product, audience, channel, and conversion goal.
Separate strategy from execution: clarify the campaign decision before drafting assets or implementation steps.
